title: Slugify a title
summary: Make clean, readable URL slugs from article titles, accents and length limits included.
prompt: The docs site builds URLs from page titles. Write `slugify(title: string, maxLength: number = 60): string`:
- Lowercase. Accented letters lose their accents: `Crème brûlée` -> `creme-brulee`.
- Every run of characters that are not `a-z` or `0-9` becomes a **single** `-`.
- No leading or trailing `-`. A title with no letters or digits gives `""`.
- If the slug is longer than `maxLength`, cut it at the **last `-` that keeps it within the limit**, so no word
is cut in half. Only when the first word alone is too long, cut that word at `maxLength`.
slugify("Quarterly report for the platform team", 18)   // "quarterly-report"
Tip: `text.normalize("NFKD")` splits `é` into `e` plus a combining accent, and `/\p{M}/gu` matches the accents.

hints: Chain the steps: `normalize("NFKD")`, remove `\p{M}` marks, lowercase, replace `[^a-z0-9]+` with `-`, trim dashes.
For the limit, look at the first `maxLength + 1` characters: if that last extra character is a dash, the cut falls exactly between words.
`lastIndexOf("-")` in that slice gives the cut point; `-1` (or `0`) means a single long word, so slice at `maxLength`.
